QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_30

question.text: Which of the following are examples of liquid assets accepted as collateral for margin purposes in IRD?

answer.text: Cash, Fixed Deposit Receipts (FDRs), Government Securities, bank guarantees, and (as non-cash) approved equity shares and corporate bonds subject to haircuts and limits
Any securities listed on the exchange without restriction
Cash only, with corporate bonds and equity shares specifically prohibited

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 257 of the NISM Series IV workbook, liquid assets accepted as collateral include cash, bank guarantees, fixed deposit receipts, approved securities, and other prescribed collateral. Government of India securities are classified in the cash component. Pages 258-260 additionally allow equity shares and corporate bonds as other liquid assets, subject to criteria and limits, with at least 50% of liquid assets required to be in the cash component / cash equivalents. The Trap: Cash-only is too narrow; the workbook accepts a broader liquid-asset list. Not every listed security qualifies; only approved securities meeting criteria and limits are accepted. Corporate bonds and equity shares are not prohibited; they are permitted as non-cash liquid assets within prescribed limits. Note: Source-backed split per pages 257-260 of Series IV: cash component (cash, FDRs, bank guarantees, GOI securities) plus non-cash component (approved equity shares and corporate bonds), with the cash component at least 50% of liquid assets and haircuts applied.
